Subject: SLA needs + billing flexibility question

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We had a brief follow-up with procurement and the engineering leadership team. Two asks:

1) Can Redwood provide a three-tier uptime matrix with clear crediting for each band (99.9, 99.95, 99.99) and standard response windows for sev-1/2/3 incidents?
2) We're evaluating a deferred-billing model for the first 6 months of ramp — procurement wants to include a clause where 60% of the months are invoiced immediately, 40% deferred and billed at the end of Q3, contingent on usage and reliability. Is that something you can support, and what discount mechanics would you apply?

I've attached our SLA request doc (Zephyr_SLA_Request_20260531.pdf) for reference.

Appreciate a quick read — our procurement cycle is tight.

Tom
Sr. IT Procurement
Zephyr Health

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA needs + billing flexibility question

Tom / Asha —

Thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the request doc. We can support both a tiered uptime matrix and a deferred-billing construct, but there are a few tradeoffs to call out up front so we can align expectations:

- Uptime bands: we can publish credit slabs at 99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99 with proportional monthly credits (higher credits for lower uptime). We typically pair the higher SLAs with a modest commit or reserved capacity to keep unit economics aligned.
- Response windows: standard offering is 1 hour sev-1, 4 hours sev-2, 24 hours sev-3 (business hours) with an option to 24/7 for sev-1 at an uplift.
- Deferred billing: we have piloted deferred billing on a case-by-case basis. A common structure is: 60% invoiced monthly, 40% deferred and billed at a milestone (end of quarter) — the deferred portion can be tied to either a) an upfront smaller discount and a larger committed discount once ramp thresholds are met, or b) an amortized credit if reliability thresholds aren't hit.

I'll draft a short pricing play with two options (commit-first vs. pay-as-you-go with deferred tranche) and loop in Marissa for the discount scaffolding and Jordan for operational requirements (oncall, escalation paths). Expect a proposal by EOD Thursday.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 08:43:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: pricing sketch for Zephyr - deferred billing and SLA bands

Team —

Quick draft of constructs we can offer. I'll put numbers in a spreadsheet (see soojin_proposal_v1.xlsx) but want feedback on structure before we send to Tom/Asha: 

Option A (Commit + Reduced Deferred):
- 12-month term, monthly invoicing. Customer commits to a target monthly throughput (reserved units).
- Uptime bands: 99.99 (0.5% monthly credit), 99.95 (1.5% credit), 99.9 (5% credit).
- Pricing: 12% volume discount on model units for committed capacity. Deferred billing: 30% of month can be deferred for first 3 months; deferred balance billed end of Q3. If uptime >= 99.95 during ramp period, deferred portion converts to standard invoice (no penalty). If uptime < 99.95, we apply a 10% amortized credit to deferred principal.

Option B (Pay-as-you-go + Deferred tranche):
- No reserved commit; higher per-unit rate.
- Uptime bands same as above but credit multipliers are 1.5x relative to Option A.
- Deferred billing: 40% of monthly invoice deferred for first 6 months. Deferred amount accrues an eligibility discount: if ramp volumes > 75% of forecast and uptime >= 99.95, customer receives a 5% bill-back rebate applied when deferred portion is invoiced. Otherwise deferred portion billed + credit offsets for shortfall.

Operational / escalation asks (Jordan): we will need to guarantee a named escalation contact for Zephyr, on-call coverage hours, and a canary fallback model (route to secondary model variant) if we hit sustained capacity constraints. That should be baked into the SLA appendix.

Thoughts? I kept the math conservative because deferred billing raises collection and credit risk for us.

—Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 10:17:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Internal: pricing sketch for Zephyr - deferred billing and SLA bands

Agree with the conservative approach. A couple of operational clarifications to include before we send to Zephyr: 

1) Escalation coverage — provide 24/7 on-call for Sev-1 with 1-hour callback, named on-call roster, and a weekly executive skip-level for the first 90 days.
2) Canary fallback — define an automatic fallback to a slightly lower-cost quantized model (same API surface) after 10 minutes sustained queue depth above threshold; this protects availability but needs to be explicit so Zephyr can test failover behavior.
3) Auditability — include a link to our uptime reporting dashboard and commit to monthly SLA reporting; provide a monthly credit calculation CSV attached to invoices so procurement can reconcile deferred tranches.

If we're comfortable with the potential DSO hit, Option B is higher risk but gives Zephyr procurement flexibility. We should ask for a stop-loss cap on deferred balance (e.g., deferred amount cannot exceed 2x average monthly run-rate) to limit exposure.

Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
